learn.title: A fixed size is a limit
learn.body: A C array like `int a[3]` has a size fixed when you write the program. If you need room for a number of items known only at run time, ask the heap with `malloc`. That gives a dynamic array you can resize.

learn.title: Allocating on the heap
learn.body: `malloc(n * sizeof *a)` returns space for n ints, or NULL on failure. `realloc` resizes the block and may move it, so always store its result. When you finish, call `free` exactly once on the pointer.

learn.title: Growing by doubling
learn.body: When the array is full, double its capacity. Real code also checks malloc and realloc for NULL.

learn.title: Tracing the growth
learn.body: Start with cap 2 and add five values.
steps: Values 0 and 10 fit. len is 2, cap is 2
Adding 20 finds the array full, so cap becomes 4
It ends with len 5 and cap 8

learn.body: Doubling means copies are rare. Most appends just write one slot.

questions.prompt: Which is a limit of `int a[3]`?
choices: Its size is fixed in the program
It lives only on the heap
questions.explanation: A plain array has a size set at compile time. A malloc'd block can be sized at run time.

questions.prompt: Why store the result of `realloc` in the pointer?
choices: It frees the old block twice
questions.explanation: realloc may move the data to a new place, so the old address can become invalid.

questions.prompt: Memory from `malloc` must be released with \_\_.
questions.explanation: Every successful malloc should be matched by exactly one free.

questions.prompt: A dynamic array has cap 2 and doubles when full. What cap does it have after holding 5 items?
questions.explanation: 2 becomes 4 at the third item, then 8 at the fifth item.

questions.prompt: What does `malloc` return when it cannot get memory?
questions.explanation: Check for NULL before using the pointer.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to grow a full dynamic array.
steps: Call realloc with the new size
questions.explanation: Make room first, then store. Using the slot before realloc would write past the end.
